post.description: "Is lodash 4.17.15 vulnerable?", "what should I upgrade to": one package at a time. Use query_batch for a dependency list and vuln for the full record of one id.

commit.description: Full Git commit hash: vulnerabilities whose affected ranges include it (C/C++ and other source-level records). Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous answer for the same query (OSV.dev page token).

ecosystem.description: OSV ecosystem: npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, crates.io, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist, Pub, Hex, Hackage, CRAN, GitHub Actions, or a distribution with release (Debian:12, Alpine:v3.20, Ubuntu:22.04:LTS). Case-insensitive; cargo, golang, gem and composer are accepted. Use with `name`.

include_details.description: Add each record's full Markdown description (`details`); off by default to keep answers small.

name.description: Package name in the ecosystem: `lodash`, `jinja2`, `golang.org/x/net`, `org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core` (Maven group:artifact).

purl.description: Package URL instead of ecosystem+name, optionally with the version: pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.15, pkg:maven/org.apache.logging.log4j/log4j-core@2.14.1.

version.description: Exact version to check (4.17.15). Omit to list every vulnerability recorded for the package.

200.description:
Known vulnerabilities affecting one package version (or every version) across npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, crates.io, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist, Linux distributions and more, from OSV.dev POST /v1/query. Accepts ecosystem+name(+version), a purl, or a Git commit. Each result gives the id and aliases (CVE/GHSA), summary, severity (CVSS vectors and the source rating), CWE ids, the affected ranges for the queried package, the versions that fix it, and per-source attribution and licence. An empty list means OSV.dev knows no vulnerability for that query.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attribution` | string | Attribution notice for OSV.dev and its source databases; keep it with the data (CC-BY 4.0 and the other source licences require attribution). |
| `count` | number |  |
| `next_cursor` | string | Pass as `cursor` with the same query for the next page (large distribution queries page at about 1000-3000 records). |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Milliseconds since the Unix epoch when this result was fetched. |
| `query` | object | The query as sent to OSV.dev; keys that do not apply are null. |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `vulnerable` | boolean | Whether this page lists at least one vulnerability. |
| `vulns` | object[] | Matching vulnerabilities in OSV.dev's order (by id); withdrawn records are excluded upstream. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.attribution: Vulnerability data from OSV.dev (https://osv.dev), which aggregates the source databases named in each record's `source`. Each record remains under its source database's licence (`source.license`; null where OSV.dev does not state one). Records are reformatted here; see `url` for the original.
